title: Cache FX rates in Redis to cut currency service load
executive_summary: ECR-2026-007 adds a Redis cache in front of the FX rate feed with a 15-minute TTL to reduce currency service load, which is a straightforward infrastructure change that doesn't touch the conversion math itself. You need to run eight tests across the Currency Service: the four P0 tests TC-1041, TC-1044, TC-1039, and TC-1043 cover the critical paths of staleness checking, feed outage recovery, serving from cache, and non-blocking refresh, while the four P1 tests TC-1038, TC-1042, TC-1040, and TC-1045 verify scheduled refresh, decimal precision, rate-age exposure, and symmetry. The biggest risk is that three past defects—BUG-101 on unsupported currencies, BUG-155 on stale rates after cache refresh failure, and BUG-301 on float rounding—all hit production before and only show coverage in TC-1041, TC-1044, and TC-1039, leaving it unclear whether TC-1038, TC-1042, TC-1043, and TC-1045 prevent them too. One more thing: REQ-1005 has no attached evidence despite being the only requirement, and there's no documentation on how rate-age propagation actually works or why 15 minutes was chosen.
